After more than 2,000 hours in this game, it's genuinely disappointing to see what it has become, especially over the past few years.

HOI4 was once a legendary grand strategy game, but in recent years, Paradox seems to have completely lost its direction. Instead of meaningfully improving, modernizing, or rebuilding a decade old game, they keep pushing out overpriced, underwhelming DLCs. Maybe time for HOI5.

Worse still, they've dragged themselves into pointless historical controversies, spending more time lecturing their own player base and trying to dictate how the community should think than actually developing the game.

I wish they'd simply focus on doing their job, work closely with competent historical advisors, and put that energy into delivering a deeper, more realistic, and historically authentic HOI4 experience.

After all, we're here to play a grand strategy game rooted in history, not to be told how to interpret it.

Yes, I would recommend this game to other players. But make no mistake, paying more than 20 euros total for this game is a waste of money, which ought to eventually lead to a waste of time. Most DLCs in this game can easily be replaced by mods, which have been outperforming the DLCs so severely that the developers started hiring mod creators to make new DLCs. The game runs poorly and lacks any visible attempt to optimize the speed after the in-game year 1943. You could argue that this is a technical problem and has nothing to do with the effort of the developers, while I can argue that the game came out a decade ago and still receives money-grabbing content frequently. This review doesn't aim to disrespect the Paradox Developers, but instead to discourage anyone from ever spending money on the expansions that this game has to offer. I genuinely like playing the game, hence why I recommended it, but am sincerely disappointed by the fact that it took 10 years of hard work and development to reach an incomplete and, dare I say, outdated game which continues to charge absurd prices for disappointing expansions, which are continuously outshined by the modding community.
Cheers!

I have over 1,000 hours and I learned a few days ago that you could assist attack an enemy without having your troops move into that territory. The game is definitely a challenge but it's great for wasting time and it has a lot of things you can do. I would say the worst part about the game is that if you want to be able to play it a lot like I do you have to keep buying the DLC that come for the game.

If you have one friend who always buys the DLC and you go into a multiplayer game with them while they host it then you get all the DLC as well for the duration of the game.

Overall I'd give the game a 9/10 as I have tried to get other people to play the game.

Hearts of Iron IV is the kind of game where you blink and suddenly it’s 1945, half your allies are fascists, and somehow Luxembourg owns the Balkans. It’s a beautiful mess of history, micromanagement, deep strategy, historical what-ifs, and complete chaos. nothing beats declaring war on the United States as Lithuania which somehow feels like a reasonable rational decision or the occasional "accidental" naval invasion of Norway. basically Risk on steroids with spreadsheets. You'll feel like a genius until your supply lines collapse and then the USSR eats your army. One minute you're liberating Europe, the next you're justifying war against Switzerland for geopolitical reasons. 10/10 would pause to redo my entire army in a front collapsed panic again. this is must-play for anyone who’s ever thought they could’ve done World War 2 better.

If a good and complete game is a nice house, base game HOI4 is a good foundation, hollow and lacking many things, but you can build upon it something good. It's just another Paradox game, the lacking base game that requires many, usually most, DLCs to enhance the experience and replayability beyond an "it's alright". Eitherway, wether you plan to only buy the base game or want to get some DLC, buy them all while on sale, this base game ain't worth more than the 14,99€ that it costs during sales. As for the DLCs, I usually wait until they are at 50% discount to not feel like I'm getting robed. I do recommend it, but only during sales. And mainly focus on Expansions, since they add mechanics that you wonder how they are not part of the base game, while Country packs are in now way worth their price since they do what mods already do, and those are free and usually better.
Overall it isn't a bad game, but it's a Paradox game.
